turn1.explanation: The unit mainly detects the central face (nose, mouth and whisker area) of cats, foxes and similar small furry mammals such as the red panda, ferret, hamster and lynx, especially when the muzzle is pale or pinkish. It also responds separately to cars (sports car, taxi, station wagon), which have no clear visual link to these faces.
turn1.evidence: Nearly all of the top 20 photos have the red shading on the snout of a cat, fox or small mammal. Dark dog muzzles (pugs, mastiffs) push the unit most negative, yet car labels make up 3 of the 12 top labels, including a red Mercedes at 1307, and the car shading covers the hood or body rather than anything face-like.
